classification.difficultyReason: Explain why angles at different vertices cannot be treated as adjacent angles on a straight line.

content.prompt: Marta thinks that $x = 180° - 41° = 139°$ because angles on a straight line add up to 180°. Explain why she is incorrect.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 4, below stem on the left
spec.description: Two distinct vertices on a horizontal baseline, with separate outward-sloping rays and minor angle arcs. No dots or relationship marks.
spec.mathematics: The marked angles do not form a straight angle at a common vertex. Ray directions reproduce the schematic appearance and do not specify x.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied labels 41° and x are visible.

answer.short: $41°$ and $x$ do not share a common vertex; they are not adjacent.
answer.worked: The angles do not share a vertex and do not together form a straight angle. Their sum is not established as $180°$, so subtracting $41°$ from $180°$ does not determine $x$.
